sql:
SELECT z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone, COUNT(t.PULocationID) AS cash_trips
FROM ops.zones z
LEFT JOIN lake.trips t ON t.PULocationID = z.LocationID AND t.payment_type = 2
GROUP BY z.LocationID, z.Borough, z.Zone
ORDER BY z.LocationID

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query spends most time scanning the full trips table (495k rows) to filter payment_type=2, then hash-joining 99k rows to 265 zones with a CAST on the join key, and finally aggregating. The sequential scan and the CAST in the join condition are the primary cost drivers.

plan_nodes.note: Join Type: RIGHT | Conditions: CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID | Estimated Cardinality: 99167

hypotheses.claim: A filter on the joined side sits in the ON clause of a LEFT JOIN; the join dominates the cost. (matched: left join lake.trips t on … and t.payment_type = 2)

The HASH_JOIN uses CAST(PULocationID AS BIGINT) = LocationID, which adds per-row CPU overhead and may prevent predicate pushdown or partition pruning; aligning the data types (e.g., making PULocationID BIGINT) would eliminate the cast and speed up the join.

The SEQ_SCAN on trips reads all 495k rows to apply payment_type=2; creating an index on payment_type or partitioning by payment_type would allow index scans or partition elimination, reducing I/O and scan time.

The HASH_GROUP_BY aggregates 99k rows after the join; pre-aggregating trips by PULocationID before the join (since the join is a left join from zones) could reduce the probe side cardinality and overall hash table size.
